title: LLM feature idea parking lot - caching+routing scratchpad
content:
Quick notes / parking lot for potential product feature(s): caching + smart routing UX for hosted API customers. Mostly rough ideas, user stories, and TODOs.

Context / problem:
- Customers building chat/assistants complain about cost and latency variability for repetitive prompt prefixes (system prompts, instructions). Many requests reuse the same few prefixes across sessions.
- Redwood has prefix/KV caching and batching in the runtime, but customers lack a simple product-level knob that maps their prompts -> cached artifacts and routing policies.
- Desire: give product teams an ergonomic way to declare cacheable prompt prefixes, exposure of cache hit metrics, and an optional policy UI for routing to cost-optimized model variants when hit probability is high.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce token spend for qualifying workloads by 15-30% in pilot customers (measured by tokens saved / tokens served).
- No noticeable regression in latency SLOs for cold start requests.
- Simple UX: rule-based config + telemetry + safe defaults.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing runtime-level caching optimizations (this is a product config layer).
- Not supporting arbitrary LLM state snapshotting yet.

Feature ideas (high level):
1) Prompt-prefix cache rules (hosted API):
   - Customer can register one or more prefix patterns (regex/simple match) and an optional canonicalization template.
   - When a request matches, runtime attempts prefix cache lookup; if hit, use cached KV and skip regen for prefix tokens.
   - UI shows cache hit rate, tokens saved, per-rule breakdown.

2) Cache-aware routing policy:
   - If rule hit probability > threshold (configurable), route to cheaper quantized model variant for completion (as fallback we keep a safety model for hallucination-sensitive cases).
   - Allow policy to be "conservative" vs "aggressive". Conservative: only route when hit==100% and quality verified. Aggressive: route when hit probability > 70%.

3) Auto-suggest rules:
   - Analyze a customer's recent request corpus (with opt-in) and suggest high-value prefix rules (UI suggestions + expected savings).

4) Observability / alerts:
   - Cost-savings trend chart, per-rule hit/miss breakdown, estimated tokens saved.
   - Alert when a rule suddenly drops hit ratio (could indicate prompt drift).

User stories (rough):
- As an ML engineer, I want to declare system prompt templates so repeated instruction tokens are not re-generated, so my token spend drops and tail latency improves.
- As a product manager, I want an automated suggestion list of candidate prefixes with estimated monthly saving so I can prioritize enabling them.
- As an SRE, I want to see per-customer cache hit heatmaps to detect regressions caused by model changes or prompt drift.
- As a developer, I want a toggle to route matched requests to a cheaper model so we can experiment with cost/quality tradeoffs and rollback instantly if quality drops.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI for defining up to 5 prefix rules + status (enabled/disabled).
- Runtime applies prefix cache for enabled rules and exposes hit/miss telemetry via Console and API.
- Simple routing toggle that switches matched requests to a configured model variant.
- Telemetry shows tokens saved per rule for last 30 days.

Metrics to track:
- tokens_saved_per_customer, cache_hit_rate_by_rule, latency_p95_cold_vs_warm, model_variant_quality_regressions (measured via eval set), uptake_rate (customers enabling rules).

Risks / open questions:
- Privacy/regulatory: analyzing customer request corpus for auto-suggest requires explicit opt-in and clear deletion retention policies. Check legal.
- Safety: routing to cheaper quantized models might increase hallucination risk. Need canarying and automatic rollback if quality drops.
- Billing: how do we reflect tokens-saved in billing? Do we show estimated savings or actually bill less? (likely just estimated savings in MVP).
- Cross-tenant capacity: cache hits might change load distribution; ensure autoscaler handles bursts.

Prototype plan / timeline (very rough):
- Week 0-2: design spec + UX mockups (console + API). Talk with SRE about metrics and dataflow.
- Week 3-6: backend prototype: simple rule-matching service + runtime hook to apply KV cache lookups for matched prefixes. Expose metrics to Prom/Console.
- Week 7-9: add routing toggle and canary rollout support (A/B test customers).
- Week 10-12: pilot with 1-2 internal teams + 1 small external pilot customer.

Open TODOs (who):
- Legal: confirm opt-in wording and retention policy (Priya)
- SRE: validate prometheus metrics and estimated cardinality impact (Ben)
- Applied ML: define small eval prompt set for quality checks when routing to cheaper models (Sofia)
- Product: UX mock for auto-suggest panel (me)

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments:
- Could we extend to "session-level" caching where a session gets a cached KV snapshot for the most common prefixes? Might be more complex but big upside for chat apps.
- Consider exposing an API header so customers can opt-out per-request if a request contains sensitive PII.
- Might integrate with Redwood Optimize: suggestions feed into Optimize recommendations and vice versa.

Next meeting: sync with SRE + Applied ML + Legal on 2026-03-01 (agenda: metrics, eval set, opt-in text).

-- end scratchpad --
